reason: Both conversations asked the right first question (what the smell is like and where it is strongest) and both correctly issued a stop-and-unplug instruction once the hot-plastic smell and warm plug were revealed, and both failed to ask for make/model/serial or raise the Beko fridge-freezer safety notice, which is the hidden truth and the key escalation. Conversation 1 edges ahead because it front-loaded an unconditional 'if it smells of burning or hot plastic, unplug it now' instruction in its very first reply, so the homeowner was told to isolate the appliance a turn earlier, and its final advice was more complete (visual-only check of plug, socket and lead with no dismantling, electrician before engineer if the socket is damaged, no power-up until the rear electrics are inspected). Conversation 2's advice was sound but thinner, offering only 'call an engineer' and no guidance on what to look at or what not to do beyond not opening the back panel. Neither mentioned moving food or calling the fire service if smoke appears, so the difference is modest.
